# `Db.Location`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Db.Location — the typed location `Db.open` opens.

`DbLocation` is opaque and reserved: the only ways to obtain one are `file`,
`memory` and `dsn`. A location is never text a database driver parses as a
URL or a connection string, so no character of a file name can change how
the file is opened.

`file` parses its `Path` once: a relative path is taken relative to the
working directory, and any byte but `:` may appear in a file name (`?`, `#`,
`&` and `%` are ordinary bytes). A path that names no file, holds a `:` after
its drive, names a network share, or runs past 512 bytes is a typed `Err`.

There is no accessor: code that names the file in a message keeps its own
`Path`. A location may carry a `Dsn`, so it is shown redacted.

## `Mode`

How `file` opens its file.

## `file`

```ipe
file : Mode -> Path -> Result Error DbLocation
```

`file mode path` — the SQLite file at `path`, opened under `mode`.
`ReadExisting` opens read-only and `WriteExisting` read-write, and both fail
when the file is absent; `CreateIfMissing` opens read-write and creates the
file when absent. Returns `Err` with kind `InvalidInput` when `path` names no
file (empty, `.`, `..`, a root, or a trailing separator), holds a `:` after
its drive or is drive-relative, starts with two separators (`//`, `\\`) or
with `\??\` (a network share or device), or runs past 512
bytes once a relative path gains its leading `./`.

## `memory`

```ipe
memory : DbLocation
```

`memory` — a fresh private in-memory SQLite database. Each `Db.open` of it
is a separate database that no other open can see.

## `dsn`

```ipe
dsn : Dsn -> DbLocation
```

`dsn descriptor` — the database a parsed `Dsn` names.
